additions: H1: Visual Studio Code 1.144
Release date: October 28, 2026 Stable
H2: Downloads for 1.144.0
H2: Release recap
The road to GitHub Universe (join us virtually!) is paved with lots of pull requests! So, let's take a step back and look at what we've shipped recently.
Remember when agent sessions would stop as soon as you closed your client? We built the Agent Host, a separate process that keeps your agents running, on your local machine or remotely.

With language servers in mind, we designed the Agent Host Protocol (AHP) to allow any client to interact with agent sessions. All of sudden, session continuity across VS Code, Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot App, and github.com lets you pick up right where you left off.
The Agents window lets you manage your agents across workspaces and environments from a single interface, whether you kick off things yourself or use automations to handle repetitive tasks.

By default, agents are now powered by the Copilot harness, the same harness used in Copilot Code Review, the Copilot CLI, the Copilot App, and Copilot Cloud sessions. Write agent customizations once and use them consistently across all these experiences.
If you prefer Anthropic's Claude Code harness or the one from OpenAI Codex, just use those instead with your Copilot subscription and enjoy the familiar VS Code developer experience.

As we continue to offer new models from different providers, how do you decide which one is best suited for your task? With model comparisons (aka Agent Bake-Off), run the same prompt against multiple models and harnesses to see which performs best. Prefer a hands-off approach? Use Copilot Fusion to choose the best model and orchestrate multiple models to work together for your task.
We've had vision capabilities for a while, but you kept asking for more. The wait is over, and now you can also prompt the agent to generate images directly in chat.
Chat is not always the best interface for every task. With canvas support, you can create rich, interactive UI to interact with your agents and visualize their outputs.
Coding with agents can be more than just writing code. Let agents interact with the browser to validate their results, or let them drive apps on your computer for automation and task execution.

If you need it, build it! So, we created a beautiful new Markdown editor. Instead of editing the raw Markdown, you can edit the rendered Markdown directly. And, of course, you can still edit the source if you prefer.

additions: Continue agent work from another app or device while your workspace, tools, and running sessions stay on your development machine. Use GitHub Environments to make that machine available across supported Copilot clients, or use SSH and dev tunnels to connect from VS Code.
This guide helps you choose a connection, share a host, manage remote environments, and continue an existing remote session without starting over.
To prevent this client from connecting to remote agent hosts, turn off
chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled
H2: Choose how to connect
Choose based on where you want to interact with the session and how you can reach its host:

SSH and dev tunnels provide VS Code-specific client-to-host access in these workflows. GitHub Environments provides machine registration for access across supported Copilot surfaces, not just another VS Code instance.

The files and development tools stay on the machine where the agent runs. Keep that machine powered on and reachable, and keep its agent host running. For a session hosted by desktop VS Code, keep the application running.

Connecting doesn't move a local session or copy its workspace to another machine. To continue an existing remote session, connect to the host where it already runs. For managed compute that doesn't depend on keeping your own host online, use cloud sessions
Cloud sessions is experimental and might change or be removed.
H2: Manage remote environments (Experimental)

Use the Remote Environments editor in the Agents window to find and manage your remote machines in one place. The table groups known SSH hosts, dev tunnels, and WSL distributions on Windows. When GitHub Environments is available and enabled, the Environments group also lists your registered machines, including offline ones. These are user-shared machines, not the managed environments used by cloud sessions.

headings: Choose where an agent makes changes
Work with multiple chats in a session
Other ways to start a session
additions: Start with one task, then add independent tasks as needed. This guide shows how to choose where agents make changes, monitor sessions, and review each result. If you prefer to work beside your editor, you can continue a supported session in the Chat view. Both interfaces let you direct agents and review their work.
H2: Start an agent session

If this is your first agent task, follow the agents quickstart for a complete example with recommended settings. For work in your own project, choose a task with a clear outcome and checks you can run to verify it.

Start a session for a local folder, GitHub repository, or remote workspace. You can attach other projects, issues, and pull requests as context before you send the first prompt. For work that doesn't belong to a project, start a quick chat.
To connect to and organize remote machines in one place, use remote environment management (Experimental).
For interactive work on managed compute, start a cloud session
Cloud sessions is experimental and might change or be removed.
. The cloud environment runs the task independently of your local machine. To continue it later, reopen the existing session rather than starting another task.
To start a new agent session in the Agents window:
Select New at the top of the sidebar or press ⌘N (Windows, Linux Ctrl+N). To start directly in a specific workspace, hover over the workspace in the sessions list and select + (New Session).
Select Folder or Repository to choose the primary execution workspace for the session. The first folder or repository you select determines where the agent runs and changes files.
To connect through SSH or a dev tunnel, select Remote Setup. If the workspace isn't trusted, review the Workspace Trust prompt before you continue.
Optionally, attach more context to the request:
Select Folder or Repository to attach more projects as context without adding workspace roots.
Select Add Context, and then select Issue... or Pull Request.... If multiple GitHub repositories are available, select a repository before you choose the issue or pull request.
Paste a GitHub issue or pull request URL directly into the prompt. The URL remains in the prompt, and VS Code automatically adds the item as a context attachment.

Choose an available agent harness, and optionally configure the agent, language model, permission level, and isolation mode. For folder isolation in a local Git repository, you can also select an existing local branch to check out before the session starts. The available options depend on the workspace. Learn how to compare agent harnesses and choose where the agent makes changes.
Type a prompt that describes what you want to accomplish, and press Enter to submit it to the agent.
Tip
To start a session in the background without leaving the current session, press Alt+Enter or hold Alt and select Send. The new session appears in the sessions list after you send the prompt.

The sessions list shows the session's status and change statistics while it works. Review questions and approval requests as they appear, then review and validate the result before integrating changes. For shared conversation controls, including how to steer or stop a request, see Use chat.
H3: Choose where an agent makes changes

For a workspace session in the Agents window, choose whether the agent edits your current folder or works in a separate Git worktree. Use a worktree to keep an agent's changes separate from your active workspace, especially when you run tasks in parallel.

Code isolation controls where the agent applies file changes. The permission level controls which actions require your approval. A worktree keeps changes out of your active workspace, but it does not restrict commands, network access, or access to files outside the worktree.

additions: Automations run agent tasks from a saved prompt and session configuration. Use them for work such as summarizing repository changes or triaging issues without starting each session manually. Run an automation on demand, on a recurring schedule, or, for cloud automations, in response to supported repository events. You can also start from a template or share an automation as a reusable file.
Cloud automations is in preview and might change before it becomes generally available. Share feedback about Cloud automations (opens in new tab).
For cloud automations

, sign in with a GitHub.com account that has write access to an eligible private repository. Your Copilot plan and organization must allow automations. See GitHub automation availability and permissions.
Automations and cloud automation management are on by default. If Automations isn't visible in the sidebar, check that
is on. If Run in the Cloud isn't available in the creation form, also check
. Turning on these settings doesn't grant access to the GitHub service.
You can choose to run an automation locally or in the cloud based on your needs:
GitHub service plans, permissions, billing, security, and supported triggers can change independently of VS Code. Review GitHub Copilot automations before enabling unattended cloud runs.

Automations start a run when a trigger fires. They are different from cloud sessions, where you start an interactive task and reopen the same session to continue it. Creating a cloud session doesn't create an automation or schedule.
H2: Create an automation
Choose local or cloud execution:
Create a new automation or select one of the starter templates. Starting from a template prepopulates the prompt and schedule fields.
Leave Run in the Cloud off.
Choose the workspace where the agent should work, or Chat for a task that doesn't need project files. The available agents depend on this choice.

Choose an available agent and review other configuration options like the model and permissions. For a Git workspace, you can select New Worktree and a base branch when the agent supports isolation. Learn how to choose an agent and code isolation.
Configure the Trigger to specify when the automation should run.
You can choose between Manual or a recurring schedule.
Optionally, in the advanced settings, enable or disable the use of customizations.
Review your automation settings, and then select Create.
In the Agents window sidebar, select Automations.
Turn on Run in the Cloud.
Choose an eligible private GitHub.com repository in the workspace picker. You can use a local clone or select a repository without cloning it to your machine. Public repositories aren't supported.
